rationale: Buying 24 sensors from Seletar costs USD 60K of premium and holds the Coralline Air redelivery, while waiting costs USD 45K at a four week licence and USD 105K at six weeks. The customer pool loan is cheaper at about USD 17K but needs Coralline Air to agree and adds a trace review on loaned units, which could take most of the 8 days of float. qa.answer: Four options. Buy the 24 sensor shortfall from Seletar Engine Parts (USD 60K, no slip, recommended), wait for the licence and move the redelivery (USD 45K at 9 days, up to USD 105K if the licence takes six weeks), borrow sensors from Coralline Air's pool (about USD 17K, needs customer agreement), or buy the whole quarter from Seletar (USD 100K, no licence dependency in Q4).

Borrowing from Coralline Air's spares pool is cheapest at an estimated USD 17K in loan and recertification fees, repaid from the Hokushin delivery on 20 Nov. It only works if Coralline Air agrees within about a week and the loaned units pass trace review. The cheapest option that does not depend on the customer is the Seletar buy at USD 60K.

In 2025 export licence processing for Hokushin's sensor family stretched to five weeks (PRE-08). We bought from Seletar Engine Parts distributor stock for USD 52K, covered two engines with 3 days of slip, and the licences arrived in week five. The lesson was to file licences per quarter in bulk rather than per consignment.

WO-2619 needs 28 N2 speed sensors at induction on 3 Nov. Without a licence Hokushin holds the consignment at origin, moving PO 4500018783-00010 to 20 Nov, 17 days late against 8 days of work-order float, so Coralline Air's redelivery moves 9 days to 21 Jan. Only 4 sensors are free in stock.
